title: Record that lastmile-ai/mcp-agent (Apache-2.0) is a different project from rinadelph/Agent-MCP and does not fill the coordination-tool gap
objective: Owner-directed: owner pointed at github.com/lastmile-ai/mcp-agent, correctly noting its Apache-2.0 license is fine for a future closed-source commercial sale, as a possible fit for the multi-agent-coordination gap left after dropping rinadelph/Agent-MCP (AGPL-3.0). Verified via WebFetch against the actual README: mcp-agent is a same-process Python framework implementing Anthropic's 'Building Effective Agents' composable patterns (router, orchestrator-workers, evaluator-optimizer) over MCP servers as tools -- it has no task-claiming, file-locking, or shared-coordination-state feature for concurrent agents editing the same files. It is the same functional shape as the already-deferred in-process frameworks (CrewAI, AutoGen/AG2, LangGraph, Camel-AI, OpenAI Agents SDK), not a stand-in for what Agent-MCP provided. License is confirmed fine (Apache-2.0, ~8.5k stars, active, 767 commits) but that does not change the shape mismatch. Recording this in docs/research/ai-agent-context-and-multi-agent-management-options.md so the near-identical name (Agent-MCP vs mcp-agent) doesn't cause re-research or confusion later.
validations: Verified via WebFetch against the actual github.com/lastmile-ai/mcp-agent README and license badge: Apache-2.0 confirmed, ~8.5k stars, 872 forks, 767 commits, actively maintained.

Confirmed its core purpose in its own words ('Build effective agents with Model Context Protocol using simple, composable patterns') is a same-process Python agent-building framework, not a coordinator for independent CLI agent sessions -- no task-claiming, file-locking, or shared-coordination-state feature found.

Added it to the Part 2 in-process-frameworks table (7th entry) with an explicit name-collision warning against rinadelph/Agent-MCP, updated all '6 in-process frameworks' references in the document to '7', and added it to the 'not recommended further' and recommended-evaluation-order lists.
No dependency installed, no ADR touched, no code changed.
artifacts: docs/research/ai-agent-context-and-multi-agent-management-options.md (added mcp-agent as a 7th in-process framework with explicit name-collision note)
risks: Research only; no dependency added, no ADR touched, no code changed.
